content.text: No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere in the document; the Customer right sits at the fallback notice period.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, which sits at the fallback (60–90 days) rather than the preferred 30 days, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (so the fallback three-month fee cap is comfortably satisfied). Garman's only termination rights are for cause under Section 17(c) (insolvency events and uncured material default); it has no convenience right during the term, which exceeds both the fallback (end-of-term only, 90 days' notice) and the preferred position. The only shortfalls against preferred wording are the 90-day (rather than 30-day) notice and the absence of an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Sparkling's convenience termination; these are minor sub-elements noted here rather than redlined, particularly as the term is perpetual-while-paying rather than a multi-year committed term.
